blocks.text: Spawn draws the chat (tabs, composer, say, whispers, party, guild, messages), and a world reaches into it as code: chat: scripts/chat.js in world.config.yaml names your file whose exports are the world's channels and its nametags (below). Say is the game's one chat, read in every room. A game has no chat of its own: a box it draws posts and reads Spawn's through chat:send and chat:history.

Voice is Spawn's too (joined by pressing the game chat's mic; then spatial over earshot, a ring on the talking head (player.talking), open mic until a player picks push to talk in Spawn's mic menu: hold V, or the mic on a phone; a world that binds V in inputs keeps V). Voice rings no ear or onSay: a game hears spoken words with SpeechRecognition in ui.js (→game-ui).

// scripts/chat.js: yours. Pure code over the rows of p and the reader ctx.self (state.*, place, party, guild), no calls. export const scopes = { trade: { in: (ctx, p) => true, post: (ctx, p) => p.state.level >= 10, slow: 10, waits: true }, officers: { in: (ctx, p) => p.guild !== null && p.guild.rank !== "member", post: (ctx, p) => true }, zone: { in: (ctx, p) => p.state.zone === ctx.self.state.zone }, }; export const character = "name"; // the player.state row the nametag shows: Name (@handle) export const profile = ["level", "class"]; // up to four player.state rows, one dim line under the name

in says who is in the channel and sees its tab, post who of them may write; slow = seconds between a person's lines; waits: true keeps lines for an absent player. p.place === ctx.self.place keeps a scope's lines in one copy: a reader sees a line from anywhere when in holds for them and for its speaker as it spoke. voice: true makes it a voice room too: those in it hear each other anywhere in their room, those who may post speak, others within earshot hear them. A throwing predicate shuts that player out, named once in the runtime log.

A game hears a line as onSay(ctx, line), on the speaker's body's behavior (the player template's), else the place's sim.js, else the world's: a /duel command, a password, a log. It cannot veto: post is the gate.
The world speaks with ctx.emit("say", { text, scope }): its own line in that scope (omitted = say, from where this entity stands), drawn as the world's; it rings no ear.
A chat box or a team channel a creator asks for is a scope: its name and rules theirs, the rest Spawn's.

A game presses Spawn's party and guild words where ctx.self is your player, judged as the card's: ctx.emit("partyAdd", { player }) asks a friend, who joins by Spawn's card or their press's partyJoin { player } until partyCancel { player } takes it back; partyLeave leaves yours; guildAdd, guildKick, guildRank { player, rank } land at once; the outcome is player.party / player.guild (spawn api ActPayloads). A person makes or finds a guild on spawn.co/guilds, never a game.

// scripts/player.js: yours export function update(ctx) { if (!ctx.self.isLocal || ctx.now() < ctx.session.next) return; ctx.session.next = ctx.now() + 2000; ctx.job("chat:history", { scope: "say" }, (r) => r.ok && (ctx.session.board = r.data.lines)); } // scripts/ui.js: the board const esc = (s) => new Option(s).innerHTML; export default (ctx) => (ctx.session.board ?? []).map((l) => `

${esc(l.by?.displayName ?? "")} ${esc(l.text)}

`).join("");

A letter from one player to another (clan mail, a note for a friend) is Spawn's message: Spawn keeps it (moderated, read by the receiver's bell), and the game's own mailbox shows player.mail and stores nothing. Your own body is no signed-in person: a letter or a chat line from it is refused, and a letter to it never arrives. Your tester (spawn client join --tester 1) is one, so a test letter leaves from its page.
# world.config.yaml: the two actions the mailbox sends inputs: actions: sendLetter: {} readLetter: {}

// scripts/player.js: the sender is this player, never an argument export function onInput(ctx, input) { if (input.pressed.sendLetter) { const ask = input.actionData.sendLetter; ctx.job("mail:send", { to: ask.to, topic: ask.topic, text: ask.text }, "onMailSent", { to: ask.to }); } if (input.pressed.readLetter) { const row = ctx.self.mail.find((m) => m.id === input.actionData.readLetter.id); if (row && !row.read) row.read = true; // Spawn keeps the mark across games } } export function onMailSent(ctx, result, payload) { ctx.self.state.lastLetter = result.ok ? `sent to ${payload.to}` : `not sent: ${result.error.message}`; }

// scripts/ui.js: the mailbox re-renders when a letter lands export default function render(ctx, player) { const rows = (player.mail ?? []).map((m) => `
${m.from.displayName} · ${m.topic}: ${m.text}
`).join(""); return `${rows}
${player.state.lastLetter ?? ""}`; }

ctx.job("chat:send", { text, scope }, "onChatSent", payload) // from the player's own body: text as typed (≤ 200 chars beside a slash word), slash words and moderation as in Spawn's box; scope "say" (omitted), a chat.js scope's name, "party", "guild" or "@handle"; data { scope, at } ctx.job("chat:history", { scope }, "onHistory") // from the player's own body: one channel ("say" or a chat.js scope's name) as the player's panel shows it; data { lines }, its last 50, each onSay's line with by { userId, displayName }, null for the world's ctx.job("mail:send", { to, topic, text }, "onMailSent", payload) // from the sender's own body (onInput); to = "@handle" or a Spawn id (player.userId, pa_…); topic 1–32 chars; text 1–200 chars; the callback gets { ok: true, data: { id, at } } or { ok: false, error: { code, message } }: the codes are the job's doc (spawn api ObjectAPI, job); message is Spawn's sentence, show it or your own player.mail // ctx.self.mail in the body's script and ui.js player.mail: this player's letters through this world, newest first: { id, from: { userId, displayName }, to: { userId, displayName }, topic, text, at, read, retracted }; row.read = true on ctx.self.mail marks it read (ui.js rows are a copy: send an action); [] on every other machine player.friends // ctx.self.friends in the body's script and ui.js player.friends: this player's Spawn friends: { userId, displayName, portraitUrl }; read-only, [] on every other machine; userId is that friend's player.userId everywhere await ctx.presence(ids) // where friends of this player stand now, for a party or guild the game formed, so a press crosses a player to a teammate; asked on the player's machine: [{ userId, world, room }] in the asked order; world = their world's ctx.world.id, room = its ctx.getRoomId(); both null while offline or not this player's friend; both undefined until an answer arrives (the first frames, or always where no player of its own stands); cross only where r.world is a string; ids = userIds or player.friends rows. Which friends are online, and a join to each, are Spawn's (its friends list and portal), never a world's list chat: script // world.config.yaml: "scripts/chat.js", yours; absent, chat is say alone earshot: 40 // world.config.yaml: metres a voice carries, and above ten players a said line's bubble, a nameplate and the `say` ear; with ten or fewer those three reach everyone in the speaker's place, and a voice the whole room until chat.js has a voice room; absent = 40 voiceMood: "cave" | "hall" | "open" // world.config.yaml: the reverb every heard voice wears; absent = dry voice: false // world.config.yaml: no voice chat (a menu game); absent = on player.voice = { gain } // 0 silent to the people around, 1 full nameplates: false // world.config.yaml: hides every name over a head (hide-and-seek, horror); absent = on nametag: ui/nametag.js // world.config.yaml: the tag over a head as a render function, the shape ui.js has: export default function (ctx, tag) { return html }; tag = { id, name, handle, face, said, named, earshot, talking, muted, mutual, dnd, agent, doing, hot, party, guild, ring, opacity, depth, distance }; named is false over every person for a viewer in streamer mode; tag.id is the body under the tag, and "" draws no tag over it: ctx.getObject(tag.id)?.state.<key> ? "" : html hides one player's tag, drawn again when that key moves; absent = the engine's own onSay(ctx, line) // line = { text, scope, by: the speaker's player handle, kind, at, nonce, picture?: SharedPicture }; paint picture.url, never a copy say // ears.say = (ctx, line) => … onSay's line; rings every entity within earshot: a shopkeeper answers "buy"

player.mail // ctx.self.mail in the body's script and ui.js player.mail: this player's letters through this world, newest first: { id, from: { userId, displayName }, to: { userId, displayName }, topic, text, at, read, retracted }; row.read = true on ctx.self.mail marks it read (ui.js rows are a copy: send an action); [] on every other machine

Which friends are online, and a join to each, are Spawn's (its friends list and portal), never a world's list
chat: script // world.config.yaml: "scripts/chat.js", yours; absent, chat is say alone
earshot: 40 // world.config.yaml: metres a voice carries, and above ten players a said line's bubble, a nameplate and the `say` ear; with ten or fewer those three reach everyone in the speaker's place, and a voice the whole room until chat.js has a voice room; absent = 40
voiceMood: "cave" | "hall" | "open" // world.config.yaml: the reverb every heard voice wears; absent = dry
voice: false // world.config.yaml: no voice chat (a menu game); absent = on
player.voice = { gain } // 0 silent to the people around, 1 full
nameplates: false // world.config.yaml: hides every name over a head (hide-and-seek, horror); absent = on
nametag: ui/nametag.js // world.config.yaml: the tag over a head as a render function, the shape ui.js has: export default function (ctx, tag) { return html }; tag = { id, name, handle, face, said, named, earshot, talking, muted, mutual, dnd, agent, doing, hot, party, guild, ring, opacity, depth, distance }; named is false over every person for a viewer in streamer mode; tag.id is the body under the tag, and "" draws no tag over it: ctx.getObject(tag.id)?.state.<key> ? "" : html hides one player's tag, drawn again when that key moves; absent = the engine's own
onSay(ctx, line) // line = { text, scope, by: the speaker's player handle, kind, at, nonce, picture?: SharedPicture }; paint picture.url, never a copy
say // ears.say = (ctx, line) => … onSay's line; rings every entity within earshot: a shopkeeper answers "buy"
